verses.text: Jesus said to them, “I’m telling you the truth: some of those standing here won’t die before they see God’s kingdom come with power.”
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him up a high mountain, where they were alone. There he was transformed before them.
His clothes became dazzling white—whiter than anyone on earth could make them.
Elijah and Moses appeared to them, talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it’s good that we’re here. Let’s put up three shelters—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
He didn’t know what to say, because they were terrified.
Then a cloud appeared and covered them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus.
As they came down the mountain, Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what they’d seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
They kept this instruction to themselves, but discussed what “rising from the dead” meant.
They asked Jesus, “Why do the legal experts say Elijah must come first?”
He replied, “Elijah does come first to restore everything. But why does Scripture say the Son of Man must suffer greatly and be treated with contempt?
I’m telling you, Elijah has already come, and they did whatever they wanted to him, just as Scripture says.”
When they returned to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and legal experts arguing with them.
As soon as the crowd saw Jesus, they were amazed and ran over to greet him.
He asked, “What are you arguing about with them?”
Someone from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought you my son. He has a spirit that takes away his speech.
Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes stiff. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they couldn’t.”
Jesus replied, “Unbelieving generation! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to me.”
They brought him. As soon as the spirit saw Jesus, it threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been happening?” He said, “Since he was a child.
The spirit has often thrown him into fire or water to kill him. If you can do anything, please take pity on us and help us.”
Jesus said, “If I can? Everything is possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the father cried out, “I believe! Help me where my faith is weak!”
When Jesus saw the crowd running over, he rebuked the impure spirit: “You deaf and mute spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again!”
The spirit screamed, shook him violently, and came out. The boy looked like a corpse, and many said, “He’s dead.”
But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and the boy stood.
After Jesus went indoors, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
He told them, “This kind can come out only through prayer.”
They left that place and traveled through Galilee. Jesus didn’t want anyone to know where they were,
because he was teaching his disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man will be handed over to people. They’ll kill him, and after he’s killed, he’ll rise three days later.”
But they didn’t understand what he meant, and they were afraid to ask him.
They came to Capernaum. When they were inside the house, Jesus asked them, “What were you arguing about on the road?”
They didn’t answer, because they’d been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
Jesus sat down, called the Twelve, and said, “If anyone wants to be first, they must be last of all and servant of all.”
He took a little child and stood the child among them. He put his arms around the child and said,
“Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me isn’t welcoming only me, but the one who sent me.”
John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name. We told him to stop, because he wasn’t following us.”
But Jesus said, “Don’t stop him. No one who does a miracle in my name will turn around right away and speak evil of me.
Whoever isn’t against us is for us.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever gives you a cup of water because you belong to Christ will certainly be rewarded.
If anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to fall away, it would be better for them to have a large millstone tied around their neck and be thrown into the sea.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It’s better to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go to hell, into the unquenchable fire.
There the worm doesn’t die, and the fire isn’t put out.
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It’s better to enter life with one foot than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.
There the worm doesn’t die, and the fire isn’t put out.
If your eye causes you to sin, tear it out. It’s better to enter God’s kingdom with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell,
where the worm doesn’t die and the fire isn’t put out.
Everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good, but if it loses its saltiness, how will you make it salty again? Keep salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.”
